subject: FinTechCo - Deployment mode follow-up (SSO / KMS / Logging)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Adam Garcia <adam@fintechco.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: FinTechCo - Deployment mode follow-up (SSO / KMS / Logging)

Adam / Priya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum.

Call notes / signals we heard:
- Auth: You will require enterprise SSO (Okta) with SAML 2.0 and SCIM for user provisioning.
- Key management: Customer-owned KMS is a requirement (you mentioned AWS KMS + external HSM in some regions).
- Network & data isolation: VPC peering or private network connectivity required; public-hosted endpoints are not acceptable for production.
- Logging & retention: Regulatory team requires 7-year audit log retention for certain transaction traces (we need to confirm exact log types).

Initial deployment-mode assessment:
- Hosted API (standard) — great for fast testing, but does not meet customer-managed KMS or private networking requirements.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity) — provides data isolation and predictable throughput; possible to support some KMS integrations, but typically does not include customer-managed HSM or fully private control plane out of the box.
- Private (VPC / on-prem) — aligns best with requirements around VPC-only access, customer KMS/HSM, and strict logging policies.

Requested items to scope Private vs Dedicated properly:
1) Okta IdP metadata and SCIM requirements (SAML certs, SP-initiated or IdP-initiated preference).
2) KMS details: AWS KMS only, external HSM usage, any FIPS/HSM vendor constraints.
3) Network diagram / CIDR ranges for VPC peering and whether you require static NAT / egress controls.
4) Specific logging retention policy doc or regulatory reference for the 7-year requirement.

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- Please share items (1)-(4) by EOD Wed so we can confirm whether Dedicated can be hardened or whether Private is required.
- Propose a technical workshop (Redwood SE + your infra/security) to run through KMS integration, SSO flow, and logging retention. Suggested window: Tue/Wed next week.

Attachments: mfa-checklist.pdf (workshop checklist)

Thanks — I’ll loop in SE and AM to prepare the workshop agenda.

—
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: FinTechCo - Deployment mode follow-up (SSO / KMS / Logging)

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- SSO: Yes, Okta SAML 2.0. We prefer SP-initiated for the admin portal; SCIM is required for provisioning.
- KMS: We use AWS KMS in most regions. For EU and APAC certain workloads require an external HSM (Thales) for key escrow / FIPS 140-2 Level 3.
- Networking: All production traffic must go over our VPC (VPC peering or PrivateLink). Public endpoints are unacceptable for production, but for PoC we can use a hosted endpoint behind our VPN.
- Logging: Compliance requires preservation of transaction audit logs for 7 years and immutable storage for certain audit artifacts. We also need the ability to redact PII before long-term archival.

I’ll gather the details you requested and upload a short doc by tomorrow morning.

Thanks — Adam
Adam Garcia
Head of Infra Engineering | FinTechCo
adam@fintechco.com

Subject: Re: FinTechCo - Deployment mode follow-up (SSO / KMS / Logging)

Chiming in from SE — quick technical read on options: 

- If the requirement is customer-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys + strict VPC-only production access + 7-year immutable retention with PII-redaction workflows, the Private deployment is the only turnkey solution we offer that fully meets all three simultaneously. Private gives you a customer-controlled control plane (VPC or on-prem), integration to your KMS/HSM, and local log retention policies.

- Dedicated can address isolation and predictable capacity. However, supporting external HSMs (Thales) and long-term immutable retention typically requires additional engineering controls and an SLA exception. We can evaluate, but expect multi-week workstreams and added controls (secure key proxies, egress restrictions, and audit log forwarding to your archival buckets).

Recommended approach:
1) Schedule a 90-minute technical workshop (SE + infra/security) to walk Okta metadata, KMS key policy requirements, and sample log flows.
2) Provide a sample KMS policy or HSM vendor integration notes; we’ll validate feasibility and list outstanding gaps.
3) If Private is expected, draft an initial PoC checklist (networking, KMS, data retention) and a high-level timeline (2–4 weeks for PoC).

Attachment: po_call_notes.pdf (my notes from the call)

Happy to run the workshop — Tuesday morning slots are open on my calendar.

—Dylan

Concrete next steps:
- Technical workshop: Tue 10:00–11:30 AM ET (90 min) — SE + your infra/security + our infra lead (Dylan). Agenda: SAML/SCIM flows, KMS/HSM integration options, log collection & retention architecture, minimal PoC scope.
- Deliverables before workshop: Okta metadata, KMS/HSM vendor notes, CIDR ranges for peering, compliance retention doc. If you can drop these by tomorrow morning, we’ll produce a PoC checklist and initial SOW draft.
- Procurement: I’ll ask our legal to prepare a Private deployment MSA template and preliminary SOW — we’ll share redlines after the workshop.

Attachments: proposed-mvp-plan.pdf (PoC & timeline)
